reason: The text (Nehemiah 2) explicitly demonstrates Yahweh's active involvement in helping the Hebrew people through multiple indicators: (1) Nehemiah's mission is described as seeking 'good/welfare for the children of Israel' (בְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵֽל); (2) God's hand is explicitly stated to be 'good' upon Nehemiah for this purpose ('יַד אֱלֹהַי הַטּוֹבָה עָלַי'); (3) Nehemiah invokes 'the God of the heavens' as one who 'will prosper us' in the rebuilding effort ('אֱלֹהֵי הַשָּׁמַיִם הוּא יַצְלִיחַ לָנוּ'); and (4) the narrative shows divine favor enabling the restoration of Jerusalem and the Hebrew people's welfare. The text portrays God's active support and blessing of efforts to help the Hebrew people.
